h1: The 7 Best LG Projectors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 LG CineBeam projectors scored on brightness, color, throw and portability, from a 300-inch dual-laser to a 720p pocket unit.
summary: The LG HU810PW is the best LG projector, with a dual-laser engine, 2,700 ANSI lumens and 97% DCI-P3 color. The HU85LA is the choice if you want a 120-inch picture from a short distance. The CineBeam S PU615U adds ultra-short throw in a stylish body, and the PH30N is the only pick under $200. Do not buy a portable Q-series for a bright living room.
intro: LG's projector range looks like a single family, but it is really three different machines under one brand. There are big laser home-theater units that replace a TV, ultra-short-throw boxes that sit on a media console, and small portable CineBeam models that live in a bag. Buying the wrong branch is the common mistake, because a portable cannot do a living room's job.

That is how we ranked them. Our editors reviewed seven CineBeam models, comparing brightness, color gamut, throw distance and portability, then scored each against the others in its own class. The scoring is anchored to the numbers LG itself lists, such as ANSI lumens and DCI-P3 coverage, and not to marketing adjectives.

products.name: LG HU810PW 4K 300" UHD (3840 x 2160) Smart Dual Laser CineBeam Projector
products.verdict: True 4K, dual lasers, 2,700 ANSI lumens and 97% DCI-P3 for a screen up to 300 inches.
products.description:
The HU810PW is LG's flagship in this group: 3840 x 2160 resolution, a dual-laser light engine, 2,700 ANSI lumens and 97% DCI-P3 coverage with a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The lumen figure keeps the image bright enough for a darkened-but-not-black room, and the gamut is what gives film its saturation.

It beats the HU85LA on raw specs, since the HU85LA does not list lumens or a gamut. The tradeoff is price and scale, because a projector that supports up to 300 inches needs a wall and a room to match.

This is the pick for a dedicated cinema or a large living room where the projector replaces a TV. The caveat is that a flagship laser projector has no dust-proofing story in the listing, so budget for a clean, ventilated mount.
products.idealFor: Dedicated cinemas and large living rooms that replace a TV.
products.skipIf: You need something you can carry.

products.name: LG HU85LA 120” 4K UHD Resolution (3840 x 2160) Laser Smart Home Theater
products.verdict: A Class 1 laser 4K projector that fills a 120-inch screen from a short distance.
products.description:
The HU85LA is a 3840 x 2160 laser smart home theater projector rated Class 1 for laser safety, with HDCP 2.2 support. The listing says it displays a 120-inch screen from just a short distance, which is the reason to buy it: you place it near the wall instead of mounting it across the room.

It ranks second behind the HU810PW because LG does not publish lumens or a gamut figure for it here. In its favour, the short-throw design means no ceiling mount and less shadow when people walk in front.

It suits a family room where a long throw is impossible. The caveat is that short-throw projectors are fussy about a flat wall and an alignment that leaves no room for slop, so install it on a stable media console.
products.idealFor: Families who want a 120-inch picture without a long throw.
products.skipIf: You need a stated brightness figure.

products.name: LG CineBeam S PU615U 4K UHD Ultra Short Throw Smart Projector
products.verdict: An ultra-short-throw 4K smart projector in a compact, stylish body for a media console.
products.description:
The CineBeam S PU615U is an ultra-short-throw 4K UHD smart projector in a compact, stylish design that fits your space. Ultra-short throw means it sits inches from the wall and throws up, so there is no ceiling mount and nothing for a guest to walk through.

It ranks third because no lumen or size figure appears in the listing, though the 4K resolution is stated. Against the HU85LA, it favours a compact body and a more modern design, while the HU85LA lists a laser source.

This suits an apartment or a tidy living room where a ceiling mount is out of the question. The caveat is that ultra-short-throw projectors need a very flat surface, and a textured wall will distort the picture noticeably.
products.idealFor: Apartments and tidy living rooms with no ceiling mount.
products.skipIf: Your wall is textured or uneven.

products.name: LG CineBeam UHD 4K Projector HU70LA
products.verdict: A 4K projector with a wheel-less 4-channel LED engine and remote focus.
products.description:
The HU70LA uses a wheel-less LED technology based on a 4-channel LED, which means there is no spinning color wheel to cause rainbow artifacts. It also has remote focus and zoom, and a breathtaking screen size is the listing's claim.

It ranks fourth because LED output is lower than the laser rivals above, and no lumen figure is provided in the listing. It is the pick for rainbow-sensitive viewers, who see flashes of color on single-chip projectors that use a wheel.

Buy it for a living room with controlled light. The caveat is that LED sources do not match laser peak brightness, so plan to dim the room for the best picture and treat daytime viewing as a compromise.
pros: No color wheel, no rainbow effect
products.skipIf: You watch in a bright room.

products.name: LG CineBeam Q HU710PB 4K Smart Portable Projector with Auto Screen Adjustment
products.verdict: A 4K portable that corrects the picture to your wall automatically.
products.description:
The CineBeam Q HU710PB is a 4K smart portable projector with auto screen adjustment, a portable design and a pitch of sharp contrast and impeccable color. Auto screen adjustment squares the image to your wall without keystone fiddling, which is the main annoyance of moving a projector.

It ranks fifth because portable bodies trade away brightness, and the listing gives no lumen figure. It sits above the PU600U in this ranking because the listing is more complete, and it is the better pick if you move the projector between rooms.

Buy it for rental flats, bedrooms and patio nights. The caveat is that a portable projector in a lit room will wash out, so use it after dark or with curtains drawn.
products.idealFor: Renters and patio users who move a projector often.
products.skipIf: The room is never fully dark.

products.name: LG CineBeam Q PU600U 4K UHD Smart Portable Projector 2026
products.verdict: The 2026 portable with 600 lumens, 4K detail and a place, point and play setup.
products.description:
The 2026 CineBeam Q PU600U lists auto screen adjustment you can place, point and play, 4K detail and 600 lumens that are bright and vivid. Six hundred lumens is a real number, and it tells you this is a dark-room portable, not a room-light projector.

It ranks below the HU710PB despite being newer, because 600 lumens is modest next to the 2,700 ANSI lumens of the HU810PW. Still, it is the one portable here that publishes a brightness figure at all.

Buy it if you want the current-generation portable and plan to use it in a dim bedroom or on a patio. The caveat is that 600 lumens cannot beat any ambient light, so it is a night-time machine.
products.idealFor: Dim bedrooms and patio movie nights.
products.skipIf: You need to fight any ambient light.

products.name: LG Electronics PH30N Portable CineBeam Projector with connectivity Bluetooth
products.verdict: The budget CineBeam: 1280 x 720, up to 100 inches and 250 ANSI lumens with Bluetooth.
products.description:
The PH30N is LG's budget portable, with HD resolution of 1280 x 720, a picture up to 100 inches and up to 250 ANSI lumens, plus Bluetooth connectivity. Those numbers are honest and modest, and 720p on a 100-inch screen is soft but watchable for casual video.

It ranks last because it is the only HD model and the dimmest by far, but it is also the only pick in the $100 to $200 bucket. For a kid's room, a camping trip or a first projector, that price changes the calculation completely.

Buy it as a low-risk portable for casual use. The caveat is that 250 ANSI lumens needs near-darkness, and 720p will look soft on a big screen.
products.idealFor: Kids' rooms, camping trips and first-time projector buyers.

methodology.title: Stated brightness
methodology.description: Published ANSI lumens led the scoring, since LG's own numbers are the best guide to room-light performance.

methodology.title: Color performance
methodology.description: DCI-P3 coverage and contrast ratio counted for film and gaming, where saturated, accurate color matters most.

methodology.title: Throw and placement
methodology.description: Ultra-short and short-throw models scored for living-room placement, while portables scored for setup ease.

methodology.title: Light source
methodology.description: Laser and LED engines were compared on longevity, rainbow artifacts and peak brightness.

methodology.title: Class fit
methodology.description: Each CineBeam was judged against its own class, because comparing a pocket unit to a flagship says little.

whatMatters.detail: ANSI lumens is the standardized way to measure brightness. A portable at 600 lumens needs a dark room, while 2,700 ANSI lumens tolerates a dim living room. Look for ANSI on the listing rather than plain lumens, and remember that screen size dilutes brightness, so a 300-inch image looks dimmer than a 100-inch one.

DCI-P3 coverage describes how much of the cinema color space the projector can reproduce. A figure like 97% means rich reds and greens in film, whereas lower coverage looks washed out. Check the listing for a DCI-P3 or Rec. 709 percentage, and treat vague vivid colors language as marketing.

Throw distance is how far the projector sits from the screen for a given picture size. Ultra-short-throw models like the PU615U sit just inches away, while standard models need a room's length. Check the throw ratio or placement distance, and measure your room before you decide where the projector will live.

Laser and LED sources last far longer than lamps and need no replacement bulb. Laser is brighter, while a wheel-less LED avoids the rainbow effect some viewers notice. Check which source the model uses, and prefer laser for bright rooms and LED if you are sensitive to rainbow flashes.

4K gives sharper detail than 720p, especially above 100 inches. A 720p picture on a 100-inch screen shows visible pixels from a close seat. Check the native resolution in the listing, and note the maximum screen size LG states, such as 100, 120 or 300 inches.

faq.q: Which LG projector works best in a bright room?
faq.a: The LG HU810PW, with 2,700 ANSI lumens, is the best here. The portable Q-series, such as the PU600U at 600 lumens or the PH30N at 250 ANSI lumens, will wash out with any ambient light and need a dark room.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying an LG projector?
faq.a: Choosing the wrong class. Portable CineBeam Q models like the HU710PB are convenient but dim, and a living room needs the HU810PW or HU85LA. Decide placement and room light first, then pick a model from that class.

faq.q: Is an ultra-short-throw projector worth it over a standard one?
faq.a: Yes if you cannot mount on the ceiling. The CineBeam S PU615U sits right at the wall and avoids shadows. The tradeoff is that it needs a very flat wall and careful alignment, whereas a standard projector like the HU70LA is more forgiving.

faq.q: How do I set up a CineBeam projector?
faq.a: Place it on a stable surface, point it at a flat wall and run the auto screen adjustment on the HU710PB or PU600U. The ultra-short PU615U needs a precise distance from the wall. Connect Wi-Fi to use its smart platform.

faq.q: Do LG laser projectors need bulb replacements?
faq.a: No. The HU810PW and HU85LA use laser sources, and the HU70LA uses LED, so none need a lamp swap. Clean dust from the vents occasionally and keep the projector ventilated to protect long-term brightness.

faq.q: Can the LG PH30N replace a TV?
faq.a: Not realistically. The PH30N is a 720p projector with up to 250 ANSI lumens, so it needs a dark room and looks soft on large screens. For TV-replacement use, step up to the HU810PW or the HU85LA.

finalTake: For most buyers who want a real TV replacement, the LG HU810PW is the best LG projector, thanks to 2,700 ANSI lumens, 97% DCI-P3 and a dual-laser engine. Pick the HU85LA if you want a 120-inch screen from a short distance, and the CineBeam S PU615U if you cannot ceiling-mount. Keep the PH30N for casual use. Never expect a portable Q-series to beat a bright room.
